title: Universal Physics-Informed Neural Interatomic Potentials for Reactive Chemistry and Excited-State Dynamics Across the Periodic Table
background:
Machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) have transformed atomistic simulation by approaching density functional theory (DFT) accuracy at orders-of-magnitude lower cost. Equivariant message-passing architectures such as MACE and Allegro [1] established systematic improvability on ground-state energies and forces, while foundation-scale models trained on the Materials Project and OC20 corpora demonstrated transferability across inorganic chemistries [2]. Recent universal potentials (e.g., MatterSim, ORB, SevenNet) extend coverage to most of the periodic table, and reactive variants have begun to capture bond breaking in organic systems [3]. In parallel, diabatic and multi-state neural surrogates have shown promise for nonadiabatic molecular dynamics on small molecules [4].

Despite this progress, no single MLIP simultaneously delivers (i) reactive accuracy across heterogeneous chemistries, (ii) physically correct excited-state manifolds with proper conical-intersection topology, and (iii) reliable extrapolation to elements and coordination environments underrepresented in training. Universal models degrade sharply on transition-metal catalysis, f-block chemistry, and charged or open-shell intermediates, where long-range electrostatics, spin states, and static correlation dominate [5]. Excited-state surrogates remain molecule-specific, lack size-consistency, and violate gauge/permutation invariances near surface crossings [4]. Furthermore, current architectures embed limited physical priors (charge equilibration, dispersion, spin), leading to unphysical forces in out-of-distribution regions and silent failures during long MD trajectories [6].

Closing these gaps requires a principled fusion of equivariant deep learning with explicit physical constraints (charge conservation, long-range Coulomb and exchange, nonadiabatic couplings, spin-state awareness), uncertainty quantification that triggers active acquisition of high-level reference data, and benchmarks that probe reactive and excited-state generalization rather than near-equilibrium interpolation.
challenges: Designing a single equivariant architecture that jointly represents ground- and excited-state potential energy surfaces with correct topology near conical intersections, preserving permutation, rotation, and gauge invariance of nonadiabatic couplings.

Encoding long-range physics (Ewald-summed electrostatics from learned charges, many-body dispersion, spin and oxidation-state embeddings) without sacrificing the linear scaling and local message-passing efficiency of modern MLIPs.

Achieving zero- and few-shot generalization across the periodic table, including 4d/5d transition metals, lanthanides, and actinides, where multireference character and relativistic effects make DFT references unreliable.

Building calibrated, physics-aware uncertainty estimators that detect reactive transition states and excited-state crossings during MD, and coupling them to active-learning pipelines that selectively query CCSD(T), MRCI, or CASPT2 references.

Curating and standardizing reactive and nonadiabatic benchmarks that go beyond near-equilibrium MD17/QM9 distributions, including barrier heights, charged intermediates, photochemical funnels, and multi-state dynamics observables.
